learning: If oval steering_oscillation falls below 0.2 and oval finishes hold at 12 or more of 20, keep y = 0.06. If oval finishes drop below about 12 of 20, return the lead to y = 0.05, because the lead cost reach. If s-bend and slalom still show line_loss at 1 or more with max_error at 0.06, tune kp (toward 2.8) or base_speed (toward 1.0) next. Do not change the spread.
notes: Race 2 controller with the Builder's forward lead (y = 0.06). Gains are unchanged so the lead move is the only variable against race 2.
rationale: Race 2 (entityR2B, score 356.98) is the best measured design: ±0.03 m spread, 16 mm footprints, y = 0.05, with kp 2.4, kd 0.45, base_speed 1.1 and weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]. The Builder's proposal changes only the lead, from y = 0.05 to y = 0.06. Race 3 (235.88) showed that widening to ±0.04 m cut oval finishes from 15 to 5 of 20 and left s-bend and slalom line loss at 1.0 and 1.15, so the spread is not what limits those tracks. The oval steering_oscillation was 0.31 in race 2, above the 0.2 threshold I set for moving the lead forward. I therefore keep the controller identical to race 2. The sensors sit 1 cm further ahead of the axle, so the controller reacts slightly earlier. With the gains unchanged, any change in oval oscillation or finishes can be attributed to the lead move. I expect oval steering_oscillation to fall toward 0.25 or below, and oval finishes to stay near race 2 levels (about 12 to 15 of 20). I do not expect s-bend or slalom to finish from geometry alone. If they still show line loss at 1 or more with max_error at 0.06, the next change should be to kp, kd or base_speed, not the geometry. The sensor geometry is passed through unchanged from the Builder's proposal.
